posts.author: u-ana
posts.title: A beginner's guide to SSRF
posts.body:
Server-side request forgery (SSRF) happens when your server fetches a URL that a user chose.

## Why it matters

The server sits *inside* your network. If an attacker can point it at an internal address, it will happily fetch things the attacker could never reach.

## The fix in three lines

```python
parsed = urlparse(url)
if parsed.scheme not in ("http", "https") or parsed.hostname not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
    abort(400)
```

Allow-list the destinations, refuse private ranges after DNS resolution, and turn redirects off.

posts.author: u-eli
posts.title: Why we moved passwords to argon2id
posts.body:
Fast hashes let attackers test billions of guesses per second. A slow, salted, memory-hard hash makes each guess expensive.

- Pick **argon2id** (or bcrypt).
- Re-hash on the next successful login.
- Never log the password, even on failure.

answers.author: u-ana
answers.body: Check ownership **on the server** for every request: load the order together with its owner and compare it with the logged-in user. Return 404 when they differ.

answers.author: u-eli
answers.body: Using random IDs (UUIDs) makes guessing harder, but it does not replace the owner check.

answers.author: u-eli
answers.body: Use **argon2id** if you can. If you stay on bcrypt, pick the highest cost that keeps a login under about half a second on your server, and raise it over time.

answers.author: u-ana
answers.body: Check whether the scanner can reach the app at all from its own network, and whether the callback address is reachable from inside the container.

answers.author: u-ben
answers.body: **Candidate**: one tool suspects it. **Corroborated**: two independent tools agree. **Confirmed**: the app was shown to be exploitable (for example a replay worked).

answers.author: u-dev
answers.body: Environment variables set by your deploy tool, never committed. Rotate any key that was ever in Git.

answers.author: u-cara
answers.body: Add a secret scanner to CI so a key cannot be pushed by mistake.

answers.author: u-mod
answers.body: **Authentication** is proving who you are. **Authorization** is deciding what you may do once you are known.
